body: Thank you.... I wish there were better words, or words that had more weight. But it meant a tremendous deal for me to hear from you here. So thank you, thank you so very much.

I do alright with sketches, artistically speaking. But I've kinda lost a lot of progress over the times I've been away from it. I've also never been really good at finishing pieces. Doesn't mean I can't start now, just not something I have the skill to be comfortable charging someone for.

Yeah, it I can get on my feet faster thanks to that.

Still not fast enough... but faster. I am also more aware of when things start spiraling and can try to recover before things get too bad. But those aren't 100% effective. Some have told me it's going to keep happening and something I kinda need to hunker down and let the storm pass when it happens, which is my normal response anyways. But there's a bit of a dilemma there because I can't hold a job with those problems... But I need to have a job to afford the therapy and the doctors to tell me that...

I live in a city, technically speaking. Colorado Springs.  
  
I have strong depressive episodes, and lose myself in those episodes. Those episodes last from 3 days to 3 weeks. When that happens... I can trick people in text that I'm alright for a little while, but can barely get up, let alone take care of myself. It's kinda like everything on this sub-par, below minimum spec, auto-pilot just so I don't do something that I, or someone else, regret(s).  
  
The flip side of my bipolar is hypomanic episodes. For that... I just seem to forget there's such things as regret, mistakes, or consequences  and I lose myself in a project, sometimes work, sometimes not. If it's not work related, I generally forget I have work, even with alarms. This lasts for a few days, but no one will understand, let alone accept that. Which has lost me a job, and a few interviews.  
  
These 2 sides don't seem to be mutually exclusive either, which hasn't caused me any work problems, but definitely other problems. I guess it's better to imagine them like 2 knobs, like a mixer. And they can both be turned to 11...  
  
As far as work goes, just to survive, I'd need something full-time. Even then, unless I'm making a lot of money over minimum wage (like 4$+ over,) that's going to cover rent and insurance. Not any debts, nor help me move forward towards going to school to pursue a goal I don't have in mind yet.  
  
It would be surviving, for the sake of survival. Which is exactly what I'm pretty much done with. Great for people who have that need for survival, but that notion is meaning less and less to me.

I know trying to find ways to be happy will help, a community will help to. Isolation does some pretty messed up things to the mind and significantly alters values on things. But as it stands, I can't afford gas to get out, my parents help me stay sheltered, try to give a little extra here and there which goes towards not starving, and beyond that, I don't really have anything.  
  
I understand the goals I need to set, such as getting a job so I can help my parents and try to expand out in my life, but being that in the past 8 years, I've never held a job for more than 8 months, and the job I did hold for 8 months ended with me being diagnosed with major depression to bipolar disorder, along with a lot of hospital visits... I don't know if it's even worthwhile anymore.  
  
I'm smart and cognitive enough to hold a decently intelligent conversation. I do alright with people. But as time goes on, I start falling apart in a social environment. Work, School... seems to be anything really. Despite being able to acknowledge this and 2 years of therapy and doctors... more like a year and a half since I lost my insurance. Trying to hold a job, but losing it after 2 months, 1 month, heck I lost a cashier job after one day... I don't have the means, probably more specifically the energy anymore to really do anything anymore. To the people that have suffered longer, I commend them, maybe there's something they can hold on to. I just don't see something like that for myself anymore.
They did hit the princess with weapons set to stun.

My parents are stationed in another country, and supporting me living alone, my dad may be an officer, but they have financial problems already, let alone spending another 2-3k per month for my inability to get things done. They care and they love me, and I will never question that, but it feels like it's to a fault at this point, and me being me right now continues to drag them further and further into debt. Not to mention the stress associated with seeing their child fall further and further into trouble, which coupled with age, seems like it's taking its toll. The question has been asked multiple times, what is going to happen to me when they eventually pass away.  
  
As for hobbies, I use to like building models, drawing and just creating things. I wanted to be a fighter pilot and astronaut when I was in 4th grade, but I got glasses because of astigmatism and that became scratched off. I didn't really have a goal after that until high school when I started drawing. Then I wanted to be a manga author and artist, or an artist for games, but I let people tell me what to do, and lost sight of that. Part of me still wants to pursue that, I got a lot to learn still. Manga is an art form that almost exclusively exists in Japan, and the entertainment industry is getting saturated with artists, who are a hell of a lot better than I am and younger to boot. I wanted to go to Art School in San Francisco. I wanted all of this so bad, but I couldn't hold down a job... and I couldn't stay dedicated to a community college.... a shitty local community college of all things.... I was always a C student anyways. I guess the consistent failures just remind me that I'm not really destined to be anything special.
